observations:
Torah #166 is a two-sentence aphoristic teaching with a minimal conceptual structure. The criterion for a new package proposal is: 3 or more bechina-connected concepts forming an independent domain not captured by the existing packages. This criterion is not met.

All five gap-analysis nodes derived from the source text (אִישׁ הָאֱלֹקִים, מֶמְשָׁלָה, צַדִּיק כְּשֶׁהָעוֹלָם אֶצְלוֹ, אֱלִישָׁע סְתָם, צַדִּיק בִּבְדִידוּתוֹ) are fully accounted for within the two proposed packages in torah_166_packages.json. There is no residual cluster of 3 or more concepts left over that would form an independent thematic domain.

The teaching has exactly one conceptual axis: the contrast between the tzaddik-with-community (Package 1: Ish HaElohim / memshala) and the tzaddik-alone (Package 2: Elisha stam / solitude). There is no third domain introduced — no tool, medium, narrative layer, evil force, anatomical metaphor, letter-system, or practice-cluster that would require a separate package.

Potential alternative domain considered: One might propose a 'Community / Congregation' package centered on 'הָעוֹלָם' (the world / the gathered students) and 'בְּנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים' (the sons of the prophets). However, this does not qualify because: (a) the text does not use bechina language for these concepts — they are the causal/conditional elements (eitza side: the world-gathering is the condition that produces/activates memshala), not bechina nodes; (b) even if they were counted as nodes, there are only two (הָעוֹלָם and בְּנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים), which falls below the 3-node threshold for an independent new package; (c) their conceptual content is absorbed into the compound node 'צַדִּיק כְּשֶׁהָעוֹלָם אֶצְלוֹ' which is already in Package 1. No new package is warranted.

The Torah's argument is a single move:
  [Package 2: neutral baseline] → eitza (world gathers) → [Package 1: good]
  Tzaddik alone (Elisha stam) → becomes → Tzaddik with community (Ish HaElohim / memshala)

This is the complete structure. No additional independent domain exists in the text.
